text:
sre-bot: ALERT: KVCACHE memory for hosted-runtime pool hosted-rt-eu-3 has exceeded 95% of allocatable GPU RAM. Projected OOM in ~3m if growth continues. Trigger: continuous-batching memory drift. Paging oncall: @maya (oncall). Link: https://grafana.internal/r/hosted-rt-eu-3/kvcache-memory

maya (oncall): Acked. I'm pulling up the memory heatmap and request traces now. Any recent rollouts?

deploy-bot: Deploy event: no rollouts in the last 2 hours to hosted-rt-eu-3.

maya (oncall): Good. Initial look — memory growth seems tied to long-context sessions. There's an abnormally large number of long prompts from a single route (customer token route:cust-42). p99 batch token size has jumped from 1.2k -> 21k in last 15m.

ravi (runtime): That matches a regression in continuous-batching where prefix KV retention wasn't trimmed for long prompt sessions. Two quick mitigations: 1) throttle prefetch for that route, 2) disable continuous-batching on the pool temporarily. Prefer doing both to buy time.

maya (oncall): I can apply throttles. What's the admin API payload?

ravi (runtime): Use admin API to set per-route caps and the pool-level toggle. Example (apply as-is from jumpbox):

```bash
curl -sS -X POST 'https://admin.internal/api/v1/config' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "target": "route:cust-42",
    "changes": {
      "kvcache.prefetch_rate": 0.05,
      "kvcache.max_prefetch_tokens": 2048
    }
  }'

curl -sS -X POST 'https://admin.internal/api/v1/config' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "target": "pool:hosted-rt-eu-3",
    "changes": {
      "continuous_batching.enabled": false,
      "kvcache.eviction_policy": "aggressive"
    }
  }'
```

maya (oncall): Applying route throttle now for cust-42. Patch 1/2 pushed.

ops-bridge: ACTION: Applied per-route config change. audit_id=cfg-204912-1.

maya (oncall): Applying pool-level toggles now.

ops-bridge: ACTION: Applied pool config change; continuous_batching disabled. audit_id=cfg-204912-2.

maya (oncall): Observing metrics — memory allocation has started to flatten, KV entries dropped ~48% over last 40s. p95 latency temporarily increased as batches shrink. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/d/hosted-rt-eu-3/kvcache-and-batching

ravi (runtime): Nice. Next short-term action: add a per-request token cap for the pool to prevent single sessions from ballooning KV: set `request.max_context_tokens` to 25k for pool hosted-rt-eu-3. Also schedule a restart of the worker processes on that pool if memory doesn't fall below 70% in 10m.

maya (oncall): I'm setting request cap to 25k and watching.

ops-bridge: ACTION: request.max_context_tokens set to 25000 for pool hosted-rt-eu-3. audit_id=cfg-204912-3.

maya (oncall): Customer impact: Hosted API errors spiked for ~2m window during growth. 5xx count increased on route:cust-42 and a few other high-context routes. Preliminary numbers: ~62 failed requests (rate-limited / OOM) across 3 customers, all p95 latency for the pool rose from 120ms -> 1.8s during the peak. Not widespread but hits SLAs for those customers. Notifying CS to proactively reach out.

ravi (runtime): We'll capture KV dump and look for retention bug. Likely regression in the trimming logic when prefetch triggers on extremely long prefixes. Will open a debug build to reproduce locally.

maya (oncall): Memory trending down to 66% now. If it stays below 75% for 10 minutes, I'll consider this mitigated and keep pool toggles until a runtime patch is deployed.

kevin (followup): I'm taking follow-up for the next shift. Summary for handoff: incident started 2049120000; cause: continuous-batching + long-context sessions causing KV retention failure; mitigations applied: per-route prefetch throttle, pool continuous_batching disabled, aggressive eviction, request.max_context_tokens=25k; customer impact: ~62 failed requests across 3 customers, p95 latency spike to 1.8s; next steps: runtime team to triage trimming bug, patch to re-enable continuous batching with safety caps, create postmortem.

maya (oncall): Thx — I'll update incident ticket and tag runtime team. Creating incident ticket now.

sre-bot: INCIDENT: Created ticket INC-204912 in PagerDuty and Pagerly. Link: https://incidents.internal/INC-204912

kevin (followup): I'll pickup the post-incident RCA tomorrow morning. For now, leaving the pool with continuous_batching disabled and caps in place. If memory creeps back up, escalate to page-ravi.

ravi (runtime): I'll start a local repro and push a fix branch — likely a trimming condition when prefetch triggers for >16k prefix lengths. I expect a candidate fix in ~4-6h.

maya (oncall): Marking thread as mitigated but open for follow-up. I'll hand off to @kevin.

deploy-bot: NOTE: No rolling restarts performed. Changes were dynamic via admin API.

ops-bridge: STATUS: pool hosted-rt-eu-3 memory 66% stable for 5m. Keeping throttles in place.

sre-bot: RESOLUTION: mitigations applied, customer-notify started, followup assigned to kevin and ravi.

maya (oncall): Ending active coordination. Leaving notes on the incident ticket. :white_check_mark:
